scope: Synthetic pool-header cases plus one Windows 10 19041 x64 crash dump. Not a 32-bit, pre-Windows 8, or other executive-object acceptance.

comparison.scope: selected fields only; full capability acceptance remains pending

notes: Compared fields are Offset, masked to the low 48 bits, and Name. The reference JSON does not preserve the canonical high bits.
The go test binary that produced the compared JSONL is 71df2c12c808160a999a3025e70bdba117fde49f989bde7d8327bc03f05eed06.
The scan covered 6416 kernel ranges and 387543040 bytes. It kept 4866 files, skipped 4118 objects of another type, 3 unreadable names and 1 invalid pool header, and recorded no read failures.
One reference name is the single character U+FFFD. Its FileName.Length is 1, and the odd trailing byte is retained as that replacement character.
windows.hivescan still uses PoolBigPageTable. This header scanner does not recover hives.
